e: An EventBridge scheduled rule triggers a Lambda function every morning to call the REST API and build the HTML report, and Amazon SES sends the email to multiple recipients. Glue is for ETL, not calling an API on a schedule, and S3 event notifications via SNS can't produce a formatted daily report.

Amazon EFS is a POSIX file system that scales automatically to petabytes, is highly available across AZs, and needs little management. S3 is object storage rather than a standard file system, and EBS is limited in size, tied to one AZ, and doesn't scale automatically.

S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents any user, including root, from deleting objects during the retention period. A lifecycle rule moving to Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year is cheap, and it keeps data across multiple AZs for resiliency. Governance mode can be bypassed by privileged users, and One Zone-IA is less resilient.

FSx for Windows File Server provides native SMB Windows file shares with Active Directory integration, and a Multi-AZ configuration gives high availability and durability while users keep accessing files the same way. S3 and EFS change the access method, and EFS doesn't support SMB for Windows.

Security groups can reference other security groups. Allowing inbound traffic to the DB security group only from the private-subnet instances' security group restricts access to just those instances. Security groups cannot deny, route tables don't filter by source within a VPC, and peering is for connecting separate VPCs.

A Regional API Gateway endpoint with a custom domain name needs the certificate in ACM in the same Region (ca-central-1), then Route 53 points the domain to the API. The us-east-1 certificate requirement applies to edge-optimized endpoints and CloudFront, not Regional endpoints.

Amazon Rekognition has a built-in content moderation API for detecting inappropriate images, and Amazon Augmented AI provides human review for low-confidence results. Comprehend analyzes text, while SageMaker or custom models on Fargate require much more development.

ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers serverlessly, so the company doesn't provision or manage the underlying servers while still getting scalability and availability. Options with EC2 instances require managing the hosts.

Kinesis Data Streams ingests very high-volume clickstream data in real time, Firehose delivers it to an S3 data lake, and Redshift analyzes it at scale. Data Pipeline with EMR, EC2 Auto Scaling, or CloudFront caching with per-object Lambda are not suited to 30 TB per day of streaming data.

An ALB listener rule on the HTTP (port 80) listener can redirect requests to HTTPS (port 443) natively. Network ACLs only allow or block traffic and don't redirect, a URL rewrite rule isn't an ALB feature of that kind, and an NLB doesn't do HTTP redirects.

Secrets Manager stores credentials so they aren't hardcoded, rotates RDS credentials automatically with built-in support, and the EC2 role is granted access to the secret. Parameter Store has no automatic rotation, and instance metadata or S3 files with Lambda rotation require custom work.

Certificates issued by an external CA can't be issued by ACM, so the certificate must be imported into ACM. Imported certificates are not renewed automatically, so EventBridge can send an expiration notice and the certificate is rotated manually. ACM-issued or private CA certificates don't come from an external CA.

S3 stores originals and converted files cheaply and at any scale, and an S3 PUT event invoking Lambda gives a serverless, scalable converter that you pay for only when used. DynamoDB isn't suited to storing large files, and Elastic Beanstalk with EC2 and EBS or EFS costs more and scales less well.

FSx for Windows File Server serves the cloud workloads, and an on-premises FSx File Gateway caches frequently used data locally for low latency and keeps the same SMB access pattern. S3 File Gateway options change how cloud workloads access data and are less natural for Windows file shares.

Textract extracts text from PDF and image files, and Comprehend Medical has a built-in PHI detection API. Both are managed services needing no model training. Python libraries or SageMaker models require more development, and Rekognition is not designed to extract document text for this use.

Files must stay immediately accessible and are critical, so they can't use Glacier (retrieval delay) and shouldn't use One Zone-IA (single AZ). Moving to Standard-IA after 30 days cuts storage cost for rarely accessed data, with a rule to delete after 4 years.

If processing takes longer than the visibility timeout, the message becomes visible again and another instance processes it, which creates duplicate rows. Increasing the visibility timeout (ChangeMessageVisibility) keeps the message hidden until processing finishes. A new queue, permissions, or wait time don't address this.

Direct Connect gives consistent low latency, and a Site-to-Site VPN backup is a low-cost failover that accepts slower traffic. Two Direct Connect connections cost more, VPN-only doesn't provide consistent latency, and there is no Direct Connect 'failover attribute' that creates a backup connection.

Spreading the Auto Scaling group across AZs and making Aurora Multi-AZ (a replica with automatic failover) gives high availability with minimal downtime and data loss, and RDS Proxy smooths failover for connections. Multi-Region designs or hourly snapshots are more operational effort or give worse recovery.

An NLB health check works at the TCP level and can't check HTTP application errors. An ALB supports HTTP health checks on a URL, and Auto Scaling can replace unhealthy instances automatically, with no custom scripts. The cron job and alarm approaches require custom handling.

DynamoDB point-in-time recovery lets you restore a table to any second in the previous 35 days, which meets a 15-minute RPO, and restoring a table fits a 1-hour RTO. Global tables replicate corruption to other Regions, and DynamoDB has no EBS snapshots.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps traffic to S3 in the same Region on the AWS network, with no NAT gateway or internet gateway data processing charges, and an endpoint policy can restrict access. NAT gateways, internet gateways, and API Gateway add costs.

The bastion host is reached from the internet through the company's external (public) IP range, so its security group should allow inbound SSH from that range. The bastion connects to the application servers over the private network, so their security group should allow SSH from the bastion's private IP address.

The public web tier must accept HTTPS from anywhere (inbound 443 from 0.0.0.0/0). The database tier should accept SQL Server traffic (port 1433) only from the web tier's security group. Security groups are stateful, so no extra outbound rules are needed, and port 443 on the database is unnecessary.

API Gateway with Lambda gives a serverless, auto-scaling application layer, and SQS between services buffers load so transactions are not dropped when a tier is overloaded. Larger EC2 instances don't remove the bottleneck, SNS is not a queue, and scaling after failures are detected is reactive.
